claims.text: Conventional MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials have a uniform grain structure.
The baseline MnNiSi-based materials provide a large magnetocaloric effect but have limited ductility and fracture toughness.
A thermal-mechanical treatment can create an inverse grain-size gradient with coarse surface grains and fine interior grains.
The inverse gradient can be produced using a single-step process.
An inverse gradient grain structure will improve the ductility of MnNiSi-based magnetocaloric materials.
An inverse gradient grain structure will improve the fracture toughness of MnNiSi-based magnetocaloric materials.
A gradient or bimodal grain-size distribution facilitates grain-boundary sliding.
A gradient or bimodal grain-size distribution facilitates crack blunting.
The modified grain structure increases the number of effective grain boundaries that impede crack propagation and promote ductile deformation.
The engineered grain structure retains a sufficiently uniform magnetic-domain configuration.
Preserving the magnetic-domain structure preserves the strong magnetocaloric effect.
The inverse gradient material will suffer less than 5% degradation in magnetocaloric properties relative to the uniform-grain baseline.
Grain size and other microstructural features can affect magnetic domain-wall movement and coercivity.
An excessively steep gradient or excessive grain refinement could disturb magnetic-domain behavior.
Disturbance of magnetic-domain behavior caused by excessive refinement could compromise the magnetocaloric effect.
The mechanical benefit and retention of the magnetocaloric effect will persist under cyclic thermo-magnetic loading near room temperature.
